messages:
Sam Li: Hey team — sketching a new synthetic traffic generator for the perf bench. Goal: produce repeatable long-tail shaping + realistic microbursts so apples-to-apples kernel selection and batching tests are meaningful.
Anya Patel: sounds good. what differences from our current Poisson/step ramp harness?
Sam Li: three main things: 1) histogram-shaped bursts (we can sculpt heavier tails), 2) stochastic state machine for burst start/stop (so inter-burst spacing isn't purely periodic), 3) request aging to emulate real KV cache hit trajectories.
Devon Chen: request aging? can you expand?
Sam Li: yeah — each synthetic user has a small seq history that maps to a KV cache warmness score. when we replay a prompt mix, some users are cold, some warm. that affects KV cache warmed tokens sent to kernel. we can parameterize warmup curves.
Marco Ruiz: sounds useful for kernel selection. if a model spends more time with cold KV we should prefer kernels with faster first-token latency even if steady-state is slightly slower.
Anya Patel: agree. we also need to ensure batching heuristics are exercised: steady QPS vs burst QPS should affect batch sizes and tail latencies. can the generator plug into the existing loadgen?
Sam Li: yes — generator will emit to the same gRPC harness. API is simple: a workload spec JSON + seed. Example spec: 
```json
{"users":1000, "burst_profile":"histogram", "tail_factor":2.5, "state_model":"markov", "kv_warm_curve":"exp(0.8)", "qps_target":200}
```
Devon Chen: nice. also add "session_affinity" flag so some requests reuse same KV keys across bursts. Want to see how prefix caching behaves.
Sam Li: good call — will add.
perf-bot: Perf run queued: run/1835-hist-burst-seed42 (link: https://redwood.internal/perf/runs/1835-hist-burst-seed42) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Anya Patel: for apples-to-apples we need control runs: identical seed, identical model binary, varying only kernel selection and quantization knob. Documented in the run metadata.
Marco Ruiz: let's also capture per-token kernel timer traces + batch occupancy histogram. small script to correlate batch occupancy vs per-token latency would be helpful.
Sam Li: plan: iterate in three phases — (A) microbench to validate statistical properties of generator (qps distribution, burst autocorrelation, tail percentiles), (B) end-to-end runs with kernel A/B and same seeds, (C) KV-cold/warm split experiments.
Devon Chen: any thoughts on how long each run should be? long tails need time to stabilize. I'd propose 30m steady with 1h for long-tail shaping experiments.
Sam Li: agreed, default 1h for tail experiments. we'll store per-second histograms and also raw sample tails for offline fitting.
Anya Patel: make sure to include a deterministic replay mode (no stochastic transitions) so QA can reproduce a single bug-case.
Sam Li: yes — deterministic mode via fixed seed and "deterministic_transitions":true.
perf-bot: Quick note — please tag runs with labels: kernel_meta, batch_policy, kv_profile, seed. That lets dashboard filter.
Marco Ruiz: perf regression detection — we should run a small daily sweep against a canonical seed and compare the tail metrics using the same generator spec. If regression > X% in p99, alert.
Anya Patel: X% = 10% for p50/p90, 5% for p99? maybe stricter for p99.
Sam Li: propose thresholds: p50 7%, p90 8%, p99 4%. can tweak.
Devon Chen: one gotcha: streaming vs non-streaming responses have different token emission patterns which interact with batching. Include both modes in the workload spec.
Sam Li: good catch. workload spec will include "streaming": true/false and "avg_output_tokens" distribution.
Anya Patel: do we need synthetic payloads that trigger different attention lengths? some kernels are sensitive to sequence length.
Sam Li: yes — we'll include a length distribution sampler and a "tail-spike" mode to inject occasional long-context requests.
perf-bot: Run results posted: https://redwood.internal/perf/runs/1835-hist-burst-seed42/summary (p50:42ms p90:120ms p99:540ms)
Marco Ruiz: thanks — early numbers look promising but we need the A/B kernel comparison. Sam, can you schedule kernel A (default cuBLAS-like) vs kernel B (fused attention) with same seed?
Sam Li: scheduling now. I'll post a small repro script and the JSON spec in the run artifacts.
Anya Patel: reminder: add a note in docs about interpreting batch occupancy vs latency — high occupancy isn't always bad if p99 stays under SLO.
Sam Li: yep. I'll draft a short README and put it under https://redwood.internal/docs/perf/synth-hist-bursts.
Devon Chen: awesome. excited to see if tail-sculpted bursts change our kernel selection ranking. :eyes:
Sam Li: thanks all — will follow up with the deterministic seed and artifacts.
